title: Runtime A/B gating and human runway notes
body:
Purpose:
This working note collects patterns for running small-to-medium scale A/B and canary exposures that must satisfy latency/cost SLOs while keeping a human-in-the-loop runway for manual hold/rollback. The emphasis is on runtime gating (automated + human) rather than offline experiment analysis.

Summary (1-2 lines):
- Provide a compact ops checklist and gating matrix for engineers and release stewards to use during progressive activation of inference-backed features.

Key principles: 
- Favor short feedback loops over large cohort sizes when user-facing risk is high.
- Make the failure mode explicit (cost spike, latency regression, hallucination rate, policy violation).
- Keep automatic gates conservative; human gates accept more context.
- Prefer incremental traffic (1%, 5%, 20%) with time windows and decision deadlines.

Activation runway (operator steps):
1) Preflight (T-24 hours): 
   - Sanity checks: model pinned? version artifact present in registry? (model:<version>)
   - Load test smoke: run synthetic burst (50 concurrent requests) against canary pool. Record p50/p95/p99 latency and GPU utilization.
   - Confirm telemetry pipeline: test event emitted (ab_exposure.test = true).
   - Notify stakeholders: #release-ops, #eng-llm, #product (see Slack template below).

2) Stage 0 -> 1% (T+0):
   - Flip traffic rule to route 1% of eligible users (or 1% sample_id buckets) to variant B.
   - Start 30m observation window. Use automatic pass/fail checks (below).
   - If no automatic failure and no manual hold requested, progress after decision deadline.

3) Stage 1 -> 5% (after n windows):
   - Expand to 5% with 1h windows. Monitor both model quality metrics and infra signals.

4) Stage 2 -> 20%
   - 3h windows, run full evaluation prompt set in parallel on recorded traffic (shadow runs) for drift detection.

5) Full rollout: 100% or scheduled ramp. Maintain rollback watchers for 48h.

Automatic gates (examples):
- Latency: p95 increase > 30% over baseline for 10m -> fail.
- Error rate: 5xx rate > baseline + 0.5% absolute AND request volume > 200 req/min -> fail.
- Cost: per-token cost uplift > 25% sustained over 30m -> pause.
- Safety: QA classifier score drop (avg) > 0.07 -> hold for human review.
- Quality: Named-entity-precision drop > 4 percentage points on evaluation set -> hold.

Human gates / runway rules: 
- Any automatic gate triggers an immediate human notify to oncall + release steward. The steward must acknowledge within 10 minutes or escalate.
- If an automatic gate triggers but request volume is low (< 60 req/min), steward may opt for extended observation (extra 1h) with increased sampling.
- Stewards can initiate a manual rollback at any point; they must log reason and timestamp in the experiment contract (see template).

Experiment contract (copy-paste template to release ticket):
- name: <feature-name>
- owner: <owner>
- steward: <release-steward>
- variants: control, candidate-B (model vX.Y)
- exposure-schedule: 1% (30m) -> 5% (1h) -> 20% (3h) -> 100% (rollout)
- primary-metric(s): latency p95, safety_classif_score, user-task-success (optional)
- abort-criteria (auto): latency p95 +30% 10m, 5xx +0.5% abs, safety_score drop 0.07
- human-hold-contacts: #release-ops, oncall-rotation, PM: @name
- rollback-procedure: run ./ops/revert_traffic --experiment <id> --reason "<reason>"; then notify channel and open postmortem if >10k affected users

Quick SQL probes (ops-friendly)
- Baseline p95 latency (last 60m):
  SELECT percentile_cont(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY latency_ms) as p95 FROM request_metrics WHERE model = 'control' AND ts > now() - interval '60 minutes';
- Variant error rate (last 10m):
  SELECT sum(case when status >= 500 then 1 else 0 end)::float / count(*) as err_rate FROM request_logs WHERE variant = 'B' AND ts > now() - interval '10 minutes';

Slack notification templates:
- Preflight message:
  "Heads up: rolling out <feature-name> (model vX.Y) to canary pool tomorrow 09:00 PT. Preflight tests scheduled. Steward: <name>. CI artifacts: <link>. If you can't attend, assign backup."
- Abort message (automated):
  "AUTO-ABORT: <feature-name> reached abort criteria (latency p95 +34%). Traffic reverted to control. Steward: <name>. Reason: p95 spike. Link: <link-to-runbook>"

Escalation matrix (who gets paged when):
- Level 1: Release steward (manual page), SRE oncall (if infra signal), Product PM (informational).
- Level 2: Eng manager + Security lead (if safety classifier triggered).
- Level 3: Exec (if >1% of daily active users impacted or data exfil risk).

Contingency actions (ordered):
1) Auto revert via traffic router. Confirm revert completed.
2) If revert fails: scale down canary pool to zero and route to fallback model.
3) If telemetry pipeline lost: freeze experiment, snapshot available logs, start incident bridge.

Observability checklist (must exist before rollout):
- Dashboard: p50/p95/p99 latency, 5xx, token-rate, cost-per-token, GPU utilization, safety classifier histogram.
- Drilldowns: by slice (region, device type, locale, user_segment).
- Synthetic tests: scheduled probe every 5m with golden prompts and expected output checks.

Data & privacy notes:
- Ensure sampling excludes PII-heavy sessions for automated evals unless explicit consent and encryption controls are in place.
- Use hashed IDs for sampling buckets.

Operator quick commands (sherpa):
- Start canary: ./ops/set_traffic --experiment <id> --variant B --pct 1
- Expand: ./ops/adjust_traffic --experiment <id> --variant B --pct 5
- Revert: ./ops/revert_traffic --experiment <id> --to control --note "auto-detect"
- Pause routing layer if needed: ./ops/router pause --tag <experiment-id>

Post-activation checks (first 24h):
- Run quality echo: sample 500 candidate responses and run automated triage for hallucination/safety.
- Confirm billing delta < expected budget.
- Confirm no persistent error mode in logs (i.e. same stacktrace repeating).

Open questions / followups (for next iteration):
- Should we add a TTL-based automatic rollback for sustained cost increases across region?
- Tighten the safety classifier thresholds with A/B historical baselines per-domain.
- Add canary-specific tracing spans to better correlate prompt templates with output drift.

Notes to self / steward reminders:
- If you see flakey oscillation at 5% -> 20% step, consider adding a stabilization pause (2h) between steps rather than exponential jumps.
- Keep a short human-only review window on the first production day (09:00-12:00 local) for high-impact features.

Appendix: quick checklist (copy into ticket)
- [ ] experiment contract created in ticket
- [ ] metric dashboards linked
- [ ] synthetic probes green
- [ ] steward assigned + backup
- [ ] rollback playbook validated
- [ ] slack channels notified

End of doc.

(Working draft — meant for release stewards and eng ops. Add examples and links to the canonical canary-sim notebook later.)
